Summary: Meta officially reported the release of the Llama 3.1 model with 405 billion parameters, making it the largest publicly available large language model at the time of its release. The model is available on IBM® watsonx.ai™, Amazon Bedrock, and Oracle Cloud Infrastructure. It is designed to excel at tasks requiring understanding multiple languages, writing code, solving complex problems, and using various tools. The model's impressive scale includes 126 layers of neural networks, 16,384 dimensions, and 128 attention heads, and it supports a context length of up to 128,000 tokens.

args.query: OpenAI official GPT-3 largest model parameters 175B paper

observations.content:
Summary: The sources confirm that the largest model of GPT-3, developed by OpenAI, has 175 billion parameters. This model was described in a paper published in May 2020 and is more than 100 times larger than its predecessor, GPT-2. The largest GPT-3 model has 96 layers, a width of 12,288, 96 attention heads of 128 dimensions each, and a context window of 2,048 tokens. It reuses GPT-2's byte-level BPE tokenization with a 50,257-token vocabulary. The model was trained on 300 billion tokens drawn from filtered datasets.

[1] GPT-3: OpenAI's 175B-Parameter Language Model | Ultralytics
    https://www.ultralytics.com/glossary/gpt-3
    GPT-3 (Generative Pre-trained Transformer 3) is a 175-billion-parameter large language model (LLM) that OpenAI described in May 2020 in the paper Language Models are Few-Shot Learners. It was more than 100 times larger than its predecessor GPT-2, and its headline result was in-context learning: given a task description and a few examples in the prompt, the same frozen model could translate, answer questions, or do arithmetic without any fine-tuning. OpenAI never released the weights and offered [...] GPT-3 is a decoder-only transformer with the same design as GPT-2, scaled up. The largest model has 96 layers, a width of 12,288, 96 attention heads of 128 dimensions each, and a context window of 2,048 tokens, and its layers alternate between dense attention and locally banded sparse attention. It reuses GPT-2's byte-level BPE tokenization with a 50,257-token vocabulary. observations.content:
Summary: The largest GPT-3 model has 175 billion parameters, an order of magnitude larger than the previous record holder, T5-11B. It requires 350GB of storage and 700GB memory to store in FP32. The model was trained on V100 GPU’s on a high-bandwidth cluster provided by Microsoft. The 175 billion parameters model is 10x more than any previous non-sparse language model and achieves strong performance on translation, question-answering, and reasoning tasks.
